added_lemmas.statement: For a canonical LV-SEM-ME satisfying Yang et al.'s LV-SEM-ME faithfulness and minimality conditions, Algorithm 1 returns its ancestral ordered grouping as a partition in causal group order, Algorithm 2 enumerates the legal ancestral-ordered-group reconstructions, and the minimum-edge output of Algorithm 2 is exactly its DOG equivalence class on the probability-one domain of Theorem 3.

added_lemmas.statement: For a canonical LV-SEM-ME \(M\) satisfying LV-SEM-ME rank faithfulness, \(M\) is nonminimal if and only if there are a root latent variable \(H_i\) and an mleaf child \(Z_j\) such that \(\operatorname{An}(Z_j)\subseteq\operatorname{An}(V_a)\) for every other child \(V_a\) of \(H_i\).

attestation.note: Checked directly against Assumption 3 and Proposition 2; the source notes that its rank faithfulness implies conventional faithfulness.

added_lemmas.statement: In a canonical latent-variable LiNGAM with unknown graph, let \(u\) and \(v\) be observed variables and let \(\operatorname{de}_o(a)\) be the observed descendants of a node \(a\). The total effect of \(u\) on \(v\) is generically identifiable if and only if there is no latent node \(h\) such that \(\operatorname{de}_o(u)=\operatorname{de}_o(h)\) and \(v\in\operatorname{de}^{G\setminus u}_o(h)\), where \(G\setminus u\) deletes all arrows into \(u\).

attestation.note: Checked directly against Theorem 3.3 in the PMLR paper.

added_lemmas.statement: For a canonical LV-SEM-ME \(M\), Yang et al.'s center/noise parameter rewriting from \(M\) to each member of its finite DOG equivalence class is invertible; under their continuous-coefficient genericity regime, all members of that class satisfy LV-SEM-ME faithfulness simultaneously with probability one.

prose_updates.tldr: For Yang et al.'s canonical separable, minimal, rank-faithful linear model with latent confounding, measurement error, and known labels, the note proves the exact jointly attained intervention-column image over every minimum-edge DOG reconstruction. A fixed mleaf contributes \(e_u\); otherwise the image consists of normalized retained columns from globally feasible pairs, together with \(e_u\) when the intervention label can be an mleaf. Every vector has one attaining minimum model, the cardinality bound \(q+1\) is sharp for every \(q\ge1\) by an explicit Bernoulli-zonotope separability construction, and scalar singletonness is exactly a zero/minor comparison. Exact rational completion lies in promise-\(\mathrm{NP}\), with optimization and search in \(\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}}\); fixed per-block interaction width is deterministically tractable even with arbitrarily many ambiguous groups overall. The unrestricted deterministic complexity remains open, and projected group marginals do not factor the full total-effect-matrix image.

project_justification.gap: Yang et al.'s Theorem 3 gives a generic minimum-edge DOG class and Algorithm 2 enumerates a Cartesian family, but it does not state the complete labeled joint total-effect-column image or classify exact constrained minimum completion. Prior latent-variable LiNGAM effect criteria omit simultaneous measurement-label restrictions and center-to-mleaf reassignment. Exact downstream cancellations make local edge scores invalid.
project_justification.niche: The intervention column depends only on the selected center/noise pair in the intervention label's unique recovered group, although membership of that pair in a global minimum remains coupled across groups. This separates an exact algebraic identification theorem from a sharply localized discrete optimization problem while preserving coherent joint witnesses.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the normalized reconstruction, complete jointly attained intervention-column image, scalar and joint singleton minor criteria, a universal sharp \(q+1\) cap with an explicit separable in-class witness, a faithful twelve-edge plateau obstruction, promise-\(\mathrm{NP}\) and \(\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}}\) upper bounds, deterministic fixed-width block tractability, the oracle-to-all-images reduction, and the no-measurement equivalence. It leaves only the unrestricted deterministic completion classification open.

prose_updates.related_work: Yang, Nafea, Kiyavash, Zhang, and Ghassami (2026), Definition 2, Theorems 2--3, Algorithms 1--2, Proposition 7, and Appendix A.4 supply the canonical model, corrected rank-faithfulness and minimality setting, recovered ancestral ordered groups, and probability-one simultaneous DOG faithfulness used here. Their Cartesian enumeration does not imply a polynomial minimum-completion algorithm. Salehkaleybar, Ghassami, Kiyavash, and Zhang (2020), Section 4, provide the closest normalized-column effect-image precedent without simultaneous measurement error. Tramontano, Kivva, Salehkaleybar, Drton, and Kiyavash (2024), Theorem 3.3, give the complete unknown-graph criterion in the no-measurement subclass; the reduction proposition proves agreement there rather than claiming that criterion as new. Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami (2026) use determinant ranks and nonintersecting paths for a different identification problem, and Wienoebst, Luttermann, Bannach, and Liskiewicz (2023) give linear-delay Markov-equivalence traversal; neither controls the coupled support cancellations in exact mixed-DOG completion. Maathuis, Kalisch, and Buehlmann (2009) motivate reporting possible effects without full DAG enumeration, but their local CPDAG computation does not supply globally minimum mixed-DOG pairs. The present computational contribution is therefore an exact verification/oracle envelope and a fixed-block-width algorithm, not a resolution of unrestricted complexity.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The effect image needs only the projected global-minimum pairs \(P_g\), but unrestricted computation of those projections remains unclassified. The faithful benchmark has a thirteen-edge strict coordinate trap and a coupled repair attaining the twelve-edge optimum, so additive per-group costs and strict coordinate descent are invalid. The bounded-block theorem enumerates complete assignments only within blocks having at most fixed \(b\) nontrivial groups and verifies every assignment exactly; it does not assume that a singleton candidate is legal. Population observational completeness is relative-Zariski generic over real canonical coefficient strata with source-law separability separate. Rational inputs are used only for deterministic bit complexity, with no probability claim on rational points.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The structural target is the complete joint column \(\{(\tau_\omega(v\leftarrow u))_{v\in V}:\omega\in\Omega^\star\}\), and each scalar image is only its coordinate projection. Deterministic reconstruction and image equalities hold for fixed \(W\), recovered groups, known labels, and a nonempty finite global argmin. Equality with the full observationally compatible minimum-edge Yang DOG class additionally uses separability, corrected minimality and Assumption 3, and \(\theta\in\Theta_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\); Appendix A.4's finite-class probability-one argument is used only there. The \(q+1\) joint-column cap is attained for every \(q\ge1\) by a two-row rational construction whose independent Bernoulli sources make the full mixing directions identifiable from the observed support zonotope. Exact \(\mathrm{COMP\text{-}EDGE}\) verification is polynomial, optimization/search have \(\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}}\) upper bounds, and fixed block interaction width is polynomial for fixed \(b\). No unrestricted polynomial-time or hardness classification is claimed, and no factorization of the full total-effect-matrix image across \(P_g\) marginals is claimed. Inference remains external: a supplied simultaneous region containing \(W\) transfers coverage to the union of these exact images by event inclusion, but this core constructs neither that region nor a uniform first-stage limit theorem.
